newsitem.title: UK: Retail sector in doldrums, CBI survey doesn't help.
newsitem.headline: Retail sector in doldrums, CBI survey doesn't help.

text.p: Friday's latest CBI report showing soaring retail sales in October did little to buck retail sector stocks today, which remained overshadowed by the threat of rising interest rates.
Most general retailing shares were slightly softer after the distributive trades report. Kingfisher was down 6p to 619-3/4p, Next was 1-1/2p lower at 551p and Boots was off 5p at 608p.
Earlier, the CBI said annualised British retail sales beat expectations and soared to an eight year high in October.

"I am not particularly surprised that the report shows such strong consumer confidence," said Victoria Melendez, retail analyst at Morgan Stanley. "But people are afraid that with strong retail sales the government will have to raise interest rates to quell inflation," she added.

Retail shares have been in the doldrums since the Chancellor's surprise quarter point hike in UK interest rates last week. "Some people are taking profits with the view that the seed of destruction for the retail boom is already sown," Melendez said.
Analysts commented that the outlook for the sector mirrored the scenario seen in 1988/89.
"If we look back at what happened then, the retailers were strong, sales were strong but the share prices were going south," said Melendez.
"The shares perform best when sales are still relatively weak, but beginning to get on their feet."
